source.title: Virchow2: Scaling Self-Supervised Mixed Magnification Models in Pathology
source.authors: Eric Zimmermann; E. Vorontsov; Julian Viret; Adam Casson; Michał Zelechowski; George Shaikovski; Neil A. Tenenholtz; J. Hall; David S. Klimstra; Razik Yousfi; Thomas J Fuchs; Nicolò Fusi; Siqi Liu; Kristen A. Severson

record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling investigations to pathology vision models and reports downstream benchmark performance by model size and training data scale. It does not test language-model pretraining-loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The study reports pathology-image downstream benchmark scores and describes a log-linear trend in average OOD performance with model and data scale. It does not report held-out pretraining loss, power-law fits or extrapolation tests, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Only the downstream-performance results bear on V6; reported ablations of training methods are not evidence about language-model loss scaling.
record.test_reason: Pathology vision foundation models (self-supervised ViTs). The study reports downstream tile-benchmark F1 against model size and training WSIs and describes a log-linear trend across models. This bears on V6 in a new modality. Comparisons are across heterogeneous models, not a controlled sweep. No pretraining loss, power-law fit, extrapolation or compute-allocation result is reported, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that pathology benchmark performance benefits on average from combining domain-specific methods, data scale and model scale. They also say data diversity and methods can beat pure parameter scaling, and that several benchmarks have saturated, so new benchmarks are needed to gauge further gains.
record.recipe_differences: Self-supervised vision-transformer pretraining on histopathology images, evaluated using downstream tile-level classification and related benchmarks; no language-model loss-scaling or compute-allocation recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies by task and embedding configuration. The authors note saturation or no substantial model-scale gains on some benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablations at fixed ViT-B size show that domain-specific augmentation and regularization change downstream F1 by several points (ID average +4.0 with ECT+KDE−SOL).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-recipe choices at fixed size shift downstream performance by amounts comparable to scaling steps.

record.problems: The reported scale comparisons are not controlled for all other changes: Virchow2 adds data diversity and training-method modifications, while Virchow2G also changes architecture and optimization settings. Some benchmark results appear saturated, and the study does not fit or test power laws in pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-task comparisons beyond the four explicitly reported plateau cases, the HEST benchmark scores, and the Virchow2G Mini distillation results are omitted; they do not directly measure the loss-scaling or predictive relations at issue here.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss versus parameters, data or compute.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation to larger runs.
No controlled shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Image modality, but no loss power-law form is fitted or tested.
No fitted exponents and no tests of fitting choices.
No prediction from pretraining loss, no fitted law, and no controlled single-axis scaling.

missing.what: Virchow2G vs Virchow2 gains on non-saturated OOD tasks, CLS+Mean: MIDOG 83.6 vs 80.4; DLBCL 62.9 vs 60.6; MHIST 86.4 vs 85.9.
HEST average Pearson correlation scales with model size (Virchow2G 0.350 best, H-optimus-0 0.347), though per-task results are inconsistent.
Cross-model comparison: Virchow (632M) matches or exceeds 1.1B H-optimus-0 and Prov-GigaPath on average.
Across-model scatter of average ID/OOD F1 against parameters and WSIs, described as a log-linear trend with no fit reported.

record.verdict_notes: Non-language, vision self-supervised setting, with downstream F1 only. The scaling evidence is a handful of confounded model comparisons, not a controlled sweep. Rows r7–r10 took values from the CLS-Only block while being labelled CLS+Mean; conclusions are unchanged.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model pretraining loss or loss-versus-parameters, tokens, or compute measurements.
No power-law fits on small runs or tests predicting much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token split.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Although this is an image-model study, it does not test whether the same power-law form holds for pretraining loss in other modalities or regimes.
Tests downstream pathology-image benchmark performance across models and scales, not language-model downstream tasks or prediction from pretraining loss.
No fitted loss exponents, compute-optimal split estimates, or tests of their dependence on fitting choices.

rows.subject: Virchow
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream benchmark performance across foundation models of different sizes and training-data scales.

conditions.value: in-distribution tile-level tasks; average weighted F1

rows.note: Reported as the reference result before the Virchow2 and Virchow2G averages.
rows.check: Reference value (Virchow ID average 0.944) that serves as the baseline for r2. It is not a scaling result in itself and should be folded into r2.

rows.subject: Virchow2
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream benchmark performance across foundation models of different sizes and training-data scales.

conditions.value: in-distribution tile-level tasks; average weighted F1

rows.note: The change also includes a larger, more diverse dataset and pathology-specific training modifications.
rows.check: Confounded: data scale (1.5M→3.1M WSIs), data diversity, mixed magnification and training recipe all change at once, with model size fixed at 632M.

rows.subject: Virchow2G
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream benchmark performance across foundation models of different sizes and training-data scales.

conditions.value: in-distribution tile-level tasks; average weighted F1

rows.note: The authors describe the gain from further model-size scaling as more modest.
rows.check: About 3x parameters gives only +0.5 points (0.966→0.971); the authors call it 'more modest'. Architecture, optimizer, data balancing and solarization also change. Text averages do not match Table 1 consistently: Virchow 0.944 matches the first block, Virchow2G 0.971 the second.

rows.subject: Virchow2G
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream benchmark performance across foundation models of different sizes and training-data scales.

conditions.value: out-of-distribution tile-level tasks; average weighted F1

rows.note: The authors report a log-linear trend in average OOD performance across models with model and data scale; this is not a fit to pretraining loss.
rows.check: Model-size step is confounded with optimizer, normalization and data-balancing changes. The log-linear trend is visual across heterogeneous models, with no fit.

rows.subject: Virchow2G
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream weighted F1 across models with different sizes.
rows.note: The authors state that no substantial model-scale improvement was observed on CRC beyond ViT-H.
rows.check: Values come from the CLS-Only block (97.4 vs 97.6), not CLS+Mean. The CLS+Mean block gives Virchow2G 97.3 vs Virchow2 97.4. Still absent.

rows.subject: Virchow2G
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream weighted F1 across models with different sizes.
rows.note: The authors state that no substantial model-scale improvement was observed on CRC-No-Norm beyond ViT-H.
rows.check: Values are from the CLS-Only block. CLS+Mean gives 97.0 vs 96.9.

rows.note: The authors state that no substantial model-scale improvement was observed on WILDS beyond ViT-H.

rows.subject: Virchow2G
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream weighted F1 across models with different sizes.
rows.note: The authors state that no substantial model-scale improvement was observed on TILS beyond ViT-H.
rows.check: Values are from the CLS-Only block (94.7). CLS+Mean gives 94.8 vs 94.8, matching the text's 0.948. The authors say TILS 'appears to have saturated'.

relationships.condition: Average ID and OOD tile benchmarks, Virchow→Virchow2→Virchow2G (CLS+Mean)
relationships.reason: Average weighted F1 rises with data and then model scale, though each step is confounded with recipe changes and there is no fitted law (r2, r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Average weighted F1 increases across in-distribution and out-of-distribution tile benchmarks as data and then model size grow, although training recipes also change.

relationships.condition: Model-size step on ID tasks and on near-ceiling OOD tasks (CRC, CRC No-Norm, WILDS, TILS)
relationships.reason: ViT-H→ViT-G gives only +0.5 ID points and no gain on saturated tasks, which the authors attribute to ceiling or label noise (r3, r7–r10).
relationships.display_finding: ViT-H to ViT-G added only 0.5 in-domain points and no gains on saturated tasks, attributed to ceilings or label noise.

relationships.condition: Cross-model comparison at different parameter counts (text-based, not in rows)
relationships.reason: Per the text, Virchow (632M) matches or exceeds 1.1B H-optimus-0 and GigaPath on average, so recipe and data dominate parameter count. HEST results are less consistent across models.
relationships.display_finding: Virchow at 632M matched or exceeded 1.1B H-optimus-0 and GigaPath on average, while HEST comparisons were less consistent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Average in-distribution and out-of-distribution tile benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Reported average weighted F1 rises from Virchow to Virchow2 and again to Virchow2G; these comparisons also change data scale or training recipe, so they do not isolate model size (r1-r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CRC, CRC No-Norm, WILDS, and TILS
reader_labels.reason: The reported Virchow2G scores do not improve on Virchow2 for these tasks, consistent with the authors' statement that model-scale gains beyond ViT-H were not substantial there (r7-r10).
